chunks: And from him, from al-Husayn ibn Muhammad, from Mu'alla ibn Muhammad, from al-Hasan ibn Ali, from Hammad ibn Uthman, from Abu Basir, who said:
Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) was asked about al-Mut'ah (temporary marriage): Is it one of the four? He said: No, and not one of the seventy.

key_terms.ٱلسَّبْعِينَ: The seventy (referring to a broader legal categorization)
key_terms.ٱلْأَرْبَع: The four (referring to a specific legal categorization)

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on Mut'ah being counted among the four or seventy types of marriage?
ai.summary: In this narration from al--Ishtibār, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies the unique jurisprudential status of al-Mut'ah by stating it is neither among the 'four' nor the 'seventy,' a phrase often interpreted by Shia scholars as indicating its exclusion from the standard categories of permanent marriage or its distinct legal classification. This highlights the Mu'takhi's view that al-Mut'ah retains a specific, independent ruling rather than being subsumed under general marital laws, a key point of divergence with Sunni jurisprudence which often categorizes it differently or abrogates it.
